subject.title: WhatsApp inter_session delivery requests can be wrongly suppressed as REPLY_SKIP / ANNOUNCE_SKIP / NO_REPLY

question: Should this WhatsApp `inter_session` delivery-loss symptom be fixed now with the narrow requester-return-path/message-tool contract from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97311, or deferred into the broader structured handoff contract tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/33478?
rationale: Current main still has the source-level suppression path, but the remaining choice changes model-facing A2A delivery guidance and intersects with prompt-cache stability and structured handoff design.

options.title: Review the narrow return-path PR
options.body: Treat the open PR as the current fix candidate, require the existing review blockers to be resolved, and validate WhatsApp or equivalent source-reply behavior before merge.

options.title: Defer to structured callbacks
options.body: Keep this issue open as acceptance coverage under the broader structured handoff design instead of landing prompt-level guidance now.

options.title: Request fresh live repro first
options.body: Hold both implementation paths until a current-main WhatsApp transcript proves the exact suppression still happens after the newer generic message-tool-only guidance.

recommendation.title: Review the narrow return-path PR
recommendation.body: Treat the open PR as the current fix candidate, require the existing review blockers to be resolved, and validate WhatsApp or equivalent source-reply behavior before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He has both feature-history signal on A2A control behavior and explicit scoping involvement on the related structured handoff issue.
